title: Desk Guidance: Days Counted in a Security Deposits Refund-Date Accrual
content:
The days counted in the accrual to the refund date on a cash Security Deposits deposit depend on the payment record of the service account since the last accrual period ended.

## Guidance

The days the refund-date accrual counts follow the record of the service account since the last accrual period ended, counting charges and payments posted fewer whole months before today than the whole months from that period's end to today: a returned payment in that time takes away the part-year returned days of **30** for each returned payment; no returned payment but one or more late payment charges takes away the part-year late days of **10** for each late payment charge; otherwise every day of the period is counted.

The returned payments and late payment charges are those on the deposit's Electric Service by Rate Schedule account.

## Which records fall in the count

The look-back is measured in whole months. Take the whole months from the end of the last accrual period to today; a returned payment or late payment charge is counted when it was posted fewer than that many whole months before today.

Hypothetical illustration: the last accrual period ended December 31, 2025 and today is April 10, 2026, three whole months later. A late payment charge posted January 12, 2026, fewer than three whole months before today, is counted; one posted January 5, 2026, three whole months and more before today, is not.

## Ladder (hypothetical period of 100 days)

| Records counted | Days counted |
|---|---|
| one returned payment | 70 |
| two returned payments and one late payment charge | 40 |
| no returned payment, two late payment charges | 80 |
| neither | 100 |

A returned payment decides the count on its own; late payment charges are then not deducted.
